subject.title: Show DeepSeek Platform usage with cost summary

question: Should an existing generic Cost summary preference count as consent to access the selected Chrome DeepSeek Platform session, or must DeepSeek retain separate explicit browser-session consent?
rationale: This is a persisted privacy and user-expectation contract; tests can verify either implementation but cannot determine which consent model the product intends.

options.title: Retain explicit browser-session consent
options.body: Keep the existing DeepSeek detailed-usage opt-in as the probe gate and defer the Cost summary-only experience until a separate consent design is approved.

options.title: Approve a dedicated DeepSeek consent migration
options.body: Add clearly worded DeepSeek session consent, migration behavior, and enabled/disabled upgrade proof before allowing Cost summary to control rendering.

recommendation.title: Retain explicit browser-session consent
recommendation.body: Keep the existing DeepSeek detailed-usage opt-in as the probe gate and defer the Cost summary-only experience until a separate consent design is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository ownership is the strongest available signal for deciding the intended persisted-setting and privacy contract.
